question: What fines apply for non-compliance with the prohibited AI practices?
reference_answer: Administrative fines of up to EUR 35 000 000 or, for undertakings, up to 7 % of total worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher (Art. 99(3)).

question: From what date does the AI Act generally apply?
reference_answer: It applies from 2 August 2026 (Art. 113), with exceptions.

question: From which date do the prohibitions on certain AI practices apply?
reference_answer: Chapters I and II (including Article 5) apply from 2 February 2025 (Art. 113(a)).

question: Above what amount of training compute is a general-purpose AI model presumed to have high-impact capabilities?
reference_answer: When the cumulative training computation is greater than 10^25 floating point operations (Art. 51(2)).

question: What must providers and deployers of AI systems do regarding AI literacy?
reference_answer: Take measures to ensure, to their best extent, a sufficient level of AI literacy of their staff and other persons operating AI systems on their behalf (Art. 4).

question: Is it allowed to use an AI system to infer the emotions of employees at the workplace?
reference_answer: No, it is prohibited, except where the AI system is intended for medical or safety reasons (Art. 5(1)(f)).

question: Can an AI system be used to build a facial recognition database by scraping facial images from the internet?
reference_answer: No. AI systems that create or expand facial recognition databases through untargeted scraping of facial images from the internet or CCTV footage are prohibited (Art. 5(1)(e)).

question: For how long must providers keep the logs automatically generated by their high-risk AI systems?
reference_answer: For a period appropriate to the intended purpose, of at least six months, unless Union or national law provides otherwise (Art. 19(1)).

question: Within how many days must a provider report a serious incident involving a high-risk AI system?
reference_answer: Not later than 15 days after becoming aware; 2 days for widespread infringements or critical infrastructure incidents; 10 days in case of death (Art. 73(2)-(4)).

question: What transparency obligation applies to AI systems such as chatbots that interact directly with people?
reference_answer: Providers must design them so that people are informed they are interacting with an AI system, unless this is obvious (Art. 50(1)).

question: Does the AI Act apply to AI systems used exclusively for military, defence or national security purposes?
reference_answer: No, such AI systems are excluded from its scope (Art. 2(3)).

question: Does the Regulation apply to AI systems developed and put into service for the sole purpose of scientific research and development?
How does the AI Act define an 'AI system'?
reference_answer: A machine-based system designed to operate with varying levels of autonomy, that may exhibit adaptiveness after deployment and that infers from the input it receives how to generate outputs such as predictions, content, recommendations or decisions that can influence physical or virtual environments (Art. 3(1)).

question: Which areas are listed as high-risk in Annex III?
reference_answer: Biometrics; critical infrastructure; education and vocational training; employment; access to essential private and public services; law enforcement; migration, asylum and border control; administration of justice and democratic processes (Annex III).

question: Is an AI system used to evaluate the creditworthiness of natural persons considered high-risk?
reference_answer: Yes, except AI systems used to detect financial fraud (Annex III, point 5(b)).

question: What information must the technical documentation of a high-risk AI system contain?
reference_answer: At least the elements of Annex IV: general description, detailed description of elements and development process, monitoring/functioning/control, performance metrics, risk management system, changes, standards applied, EU declaration of conformity, post-market monitoring plan.

question: What are the human oversight requirements for high-risk AI systems?
reference_answer: They must be designed so that they can be effectively overseen by natural persons during use, with measures enabling overseers to understand, monitor, interpret, override or stop the system (Art. 14).

question: What quality criteria must training, validation and testing data sets of high-risk AI systems meet?
reference_answer: They must be subject to data governance practices and be relevant, sufficiently representative and, to the best extent possible, free of errors and complete in view of the intended purpose (Art. 10).

question: Which deployers must carry out a fundamental rights impact assessment before deploying a high-risk AI system?
reference_answer: Bodies governed by public law, private entities providing public services, and deployers of systems in points 5(b) and (c) of Annex III (credit scoring, life and health insurance) (Art. 27(1)).

question: Do people affected by a decision based on a high-risk AI system have a right to an explanation?
reference_answer: Yes, they can obtain from the deployer clear and meaningful explanations of the role of the AI system in the decision-making procedure and the main elements of the decision (Art. 86(1)).

question: By when must Member States have at least one AI regulatory sandbox operational?
reference_answer: By 2 August 2026 (Art. 57(1)).

question: What obligations do providers of general-purpose AI models have regarding copyright?
reference_answer: Put in place a policy to comply with Union copyright law, including reservations of rights, and publish a sufficiently detailed summary of the content used for training (Art. 53(1)(c)-(d)).

question: What additional obligations apply to providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk?
reference_answer: Perform model evaluations including adversarial testing, assess and mitigate systemic risks, track and report serious incidents, and ensure adequate cybersecurity protection (Art. 55(1)).

question: What fines can the Commission impose on providers of general-purpose AI models?
reference_answer: Fines not exceeding 3 % of annual total worldwide turnover or EUR 15 000 000, whichever is higher (Art. 101(1)).

question: What is the maximum fine for a Union institution that engages in a prohibited AI practice?
Why does the Regulation prohibit AI-enabled manipulative techniques?
reference_answer: Because they can persuade people into unwanted behaviours or deceive them, subverting and impairing their autonomy, decision-making and free choice (Recital 29).

question: Which criteria does the Commission take into account to designate a general-purpose AI model as having systemic risk?
reference_answer: Number of parameters, quality or size of the data set, training compute, input/output modalities, benchmarks and evaluations of capabilities, impact on the internal market due to reach (e.g. 10 000 registered business users), number of registered end-users (Annex XIII).

question: ¿Qué multas se aplican por incumplir la prohibición de las prácticas de IA del artículo 5?
reference_answer: Multas de hasta 35 000 000 EUR o, si el infractor es una empresa, hasta el 7 % del volumen de negocios mundial anual, si esta cuantía es superior (art. 99.3).

question: ¿A partir de qué fecha se aplica con carácter general el Reglamento de IA?
reference_answer: A partir del 2 de agosto de 2026 (art. 113).

question: ¿Está permitido usar sistemas de IA para inferir las emociones de los trabajadores en el lugar de trabajo?
reference_answer: No, está prohibido salvo por motivos médicos o de seguridad (art. 5.1.f).

question: ¿Qué obligación tienen los proveedores de sistemas de IA que generan contenido sintético de audio, imagen, vídeo o texto?
reference_answer: Garantizar que los resultados estén marcados en un formato legible por máquina y sean detectables como generados o manipulados artificialmente (art. 50.2).

question: ¿Qué sistemas de IA del ámbito del empleo se consideran de alto riesgo?
reference_answer: Los destinados a la contratación o selección de personas (anuncios, filtrado de solicitudes, evaluación de candidatos) y a tomar decisiones sobre condiciones laborales, promoción, despido, asignación de tareas o supervisión del rendimiento (anexo III, punto 4).
